canonicalV2Format: The first line is "pulse-index-v2". Then one line per field, in the fixed order of canonicalV2Fields for the print type, joined with REAL newline characters (0x0A), no trailing newline. Each line is <path>=<value>: <path> is the JSON field name, dotted for a sub-field (interval.lower, cadence.band); <value> is that field written as JSON, exactly the text the response carries: numbers as they appear on the wire, strings in double quotes, arrays and objects as compact JSON, and null when the field is null or absent from the print. Every listed field always has a line, so a field added after signing cannot pass as signed. The print carries the exact signed string in v2.canonical, so no verifier has to rebuild it.
verifyV2: 1. Select the public key whose kid equals v2.kid.
2. ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 verify the base64 v2.signature (IEEE-P1363 r||s, 64 bytes) over the UTF-8 bytes of v2.canonical exactly as given.

3. Check the first line is "pulse-index-v2". For every other line, split at the first "=", JSON.parse the right-hand side, and compare it with the field that path names in the print (absent counts as null). Compare parsed values, never re-serialized text.

4. Trust only fields that have a line in the canonical. signature, sig, kid, v2 and request envelope fields (success, ok, sample, note, getKey, deltaMs, readMs, billedUnits) are not part of the signed record.
note: Select the public key whose kid matches the signed response. Build the canonical string with priceText exactly as returned, joining the five fields with REAL newline characters (0x0A) — `canonical` above contains them literally; `canonicalEscaped` is the same string rendered on one line. Then ECDSA-P256/SHA-256 verify the base64 signature (IEEE-P1363 r||s).
noteV2: Every print also carries a v2 block that signs the WHOLE record (sources, tier, confidence, dispersionBps, interval, cadence and engine as well as the price), with the same key. Verify v2.signature over v2.canonical exactly as given, then check each line against the JSON field it names; see verifyV2. v1 is unchanged and still verifies.
